questions.stem: An industrial warehouse robot traverses a distance of \\(16.47\\) metres in \\(9\\) seconds. At this constant speed, how many metres will the robot travel in exactly one minute?
questions.hint: First find the speed of the robot per second by dividing \\(16.47\\) by \\(9\\). Then, multiply this speed by \\(60\\) seconds (one minute).

steps.explain: Identify the given values and plan the steps. The robot travels \\(16.47\\) metres in \\(9\\) seconds, and we need to find the distance traveled in \\(60\\) seconds.
Calculate the robot's speed per second by dividing the distance by the time. This gives the rate of travel in metres per second.
Multiply the speed by 60 to find the total distance covered in one minute (60 seconds). Multi-digit multiplication is used.
State the final conclusion with appropriate units. The warehouse robot will travel a total distance of 109.8 metres in one minute.

questions.stem: Premium carbon fiber tape costs \\(\$4.70\\) per metre. How much will it cost an aerospace engineering team to purchase \\(8.5\\) metres of this tape?
questions.hint: Multiply the cost per metre by the total length required: \\(4.70 \\times 8.5\\).

steps.explain: First, identify the rate and the quantity to find the total cost. The rate is \\(\$4.70\\) per metre, and the total length is \\(8.5\\) metres.
Set up the multiplication of the decimal values. We can ignore the decimal points initially and multiply the integers, then place the decimal point.
Perform the multiplication \\(47 \\times 85 = 3995\\). Since there are two decimal places in total between the factors (one in 4.7 and one in 8.5), place the decimal point two digits from the right.
Write the final cost with the currency symbol. The total cost to buy 8.5 metres of carbon fiber tape is \\(\$39.95\\).

questions.stem: A precision assembly arm records the cycle times in seconds for assembling six components: \\(10.7\\), \\(10.5\\), \\(10.8\\), \\(10.9\\), \\(11.0\\), and \\(10.3\\) seconds. What is the average cycle time of the robot in seconds?
questions.hint: To find the average, sum all six cycle times together and then divide the sum by the total number of components, which is \\(6\\).

steps.explain: First, identify the dataset of times and the number of values. The times are \\(\{10.7, 10.5, 10.8, 10.9, 11.0, 10.3\}\) and the count is \\(6\\).
Add the six decimal times together. Align the decimal points and sum the values.
Divide the sum \\(64.2\\) by the count \\(6\\) to find the mean average. Perform the decimal division.
Conclude that the average cycle time is 10.7 seconds. This represents the central tendency of the assembly time.

questions.stem: A chemical laboratory purchases high-grade liquid nitrogen at a rate of \\(\$8.40\\) per litre. What is the total cost in dollars to purchase exactly \\(1.3\\) litres of liquid nitrogen?
questions.hint: Multiply the price per litre by the number of litres: \\(8.40 \\times 1.3\\).

steps.explain: Identify the unit price and quantity required. The price is \\(\$8.40\\) per litre, and the quantity is \\(1.3\\) litres.
Set up the multiplication of the decimal values. You can drop the trailing zero in 8.40 to simplify the calculation.
Multiply the numbers as integers: \\(84 \\times 13 = 1092\\). Since the factors have two decimal places combined, place the decimal point two spaces from the right.
Confirm the final cost in dollars. The total cost of the liquid nitrogen is \\(\$10.92\\).

questions.stem: A specialized 3D printing service charges \\(\$7.42\\) per hour of machine operation. How much in dollars will a client be charged for a print job that requires exactly \\(35\\) hours of continuous operation?
questions.hint: Multiply the hourly charge rate of \\(\$7.42\\) by the total duration of \\(35\\) hours.

steps.explain: Identify the hourly charge and the total hours to calculate the overall cost. The hourly rate is \\(\$7.42\\), and the total duration is \\(35\\) hours.
Set up the multiplication of the decimal number \\(7.42\\) and the whole number \\(35\\).
Multiply the digits: \\(742 \\times 35 = 25970\\). Since the factor 7.42 has two decimal places, place the decimal point two digits from the right of 25970.
Conclude with the final cost in dollars. The client will be charged \\(\$259.70\\) for the printing service.

questions.stem: A community greenhouse receives a utility bill of \\(\$334\\) for a heating pump that ran continuously for \\(40\\) hours. What is the average operating cost of the heating pump per hour?
questions.hint: Divide the total utility bill of \\(\$334\\) by the total operating time of \\(40\\) hours.

steps.explain: Identify the total cost and hours to find the hourly rate. The total cost is \\(\$334\\), and the duration is \\(40\\) hours.
Set up the division of the total cost by the number of hours. This can be simplified by dividing by 10 first, then by 4.
Divide the numerator and denominator by 10 to simplify the fraction. This makes the divisor a single digit.
Perform long division of \\(33.4\\) by \\(4\\) to get the final decimal quotient.
Express the result in currency terms. The average operating cost of the heating pump is \\(\$8.35\\) per hour.

questions.stem: A solar energy storage system feeds electricity back into the grid, returning \\(32\\) cents of credit for every dollar value of energy produced. How much credit in dollars will a household receive if their total produced energy value is \\(\$350.00\\)?
questions.hint: Express the 32 cents tax/credit rate as a decimal value of \\(0.32\\) per dollar, then multiply by the total value of \\(\$350.00\\).

steps.explain: Identify the credit rate and the total energy value. The rate is \\(32\\) cents per dollar (which is \\(\$0.32\\) per dollar), and the total value is \\(\$350\\).
Set up the multiplication of the total energy value and the decimal rate. This determines the total credits earned.
Multiply the numbers as integers first: \\(350 \\times 32 = 11200\\). Since the rate has two decimal places, move the decimal point two places to the left.
Confirm the final credit amount. The household will receive a total credit of \\(\$112.00\\).
